chift_routes.one_line: Workaround (D11): native endpoint, but amounts are stored in EUR only (foreign-currency operations converted at the supplied rate) and operation numbers must be numeric. Maps to POST /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new, which posts an OD into a daybook of Type 600, the only type auto-selected and validated (D6). Each signed Chift amount is split into Debit/Credit and the line type becomes Type 1/2/3. Extra calls: per-folder daybook and analytics caches (D8), a fiscal-years.list closure check before every create (closure dates read fresh), a book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo duplicate pre-check whenever operation_number is supplied (D12; its fiscal-year period comes from the closure-check call), and a GET /book-entries.info read-back (Folder.Id checked, D13) when Horus generates the number. Lines are sent in line_number order. Entries confirmed in Horus (direct posting mode, D12) cannot be deleted through the API.

summary: Chift 'Create miscellaneous operation' maps onto the dedicated Horus POST /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new ("Insert a miscellaneous operation (OD). The result will contain the generated book entry's id."), posted as application/json into a daybook of Type 600 (MiscOperation), the only daybook type this route auto-selects or accepts (D6). The payload needs only deterministic transformations: each signed Chift amount, normalised once (converted to EUR at the supplied rate when the operation is in another currency, then rounded to 2 decimals), becomes the non-negative Debit/Credit columns (positive = Credit), the line type becomes Type 1/2/3, partner_id becomes CompanyId on customer/supplier lines, status becomes Confirmed according to the per-connection posting mode (D12: review mode, the proposed default, pushes every operation unconfirmed; direct mode confirms 'posted' operations) plus AutoGenerateNumber when a confirmed operation has no number, the date gets a time and offset, and analytic_account (a cost-section GUID) becomes one CostLine whose schema and section search keys come from the per-folder analytics cache (D8). The call pattern is: resolve the folder (D7) and the cached reference data (daybooks.list; cost-schemas.list + cost-sections.list with IncludeInactive=true; optional accounts/companies checks with Folder.Id guards, D13); check the closure dates with a fresh fiscal-years.list call, as Horus recommends; when operation_number is supplied, run a book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo duplicate pre-check over that fiscal year (D12); post; then, only when Horus generated the number, read back with GET /book-entries.info?Id= and check its Folder.Id (D13). The verdict is workaround under D11: amounts are stored in EUR only (foreign-currency operations are converted at the supplied rate and the original currency is not kept), operation numbers must be numeric, and returning a Horus-generated number needs a read-back. The duplicate pre-check on a supplied number is a connector safeguard, and the line order is preserved. Other risks: Horus refuses unbalanced ODs and has no AllowUnbalanced option on this endpoint, in direct mode a 'posted' operation is confirmed and can no longer be deleted through the API, updates create a new book-entry Id, and there is no idempotency key, so a timeout must be followed by a best-effort duplicate check and never by a blind retry.
verdict_rationale:
Supported with workaround, under the verdict definitions of section 2 (D11). Horus has a native write endpoint built for this business object: an OD in a MiscOperation daybook, Type 600 (Guide: Data model table "Miscellaneous operation 600 book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new"), and every required Chift field maps with a deterministic transformation: amount sign → Debit/Credit, type enum → Type, date → date-time, status → Confirmed (D12).

It is not 'supported' because of constraints Horus imposes:
- Currency: the misc-op body has no currency or rate field (D), so amounts are stored in EUR. Foreign-currency operations are converted at the supplied rate (by Chift core or by the connector; question to Chift) and the original currency is not kept in Horus.
- Numbering: Horus Number is numeric ("Number *: number"), so alphanumeric operation_number values cannot be stored as the entry number (handling: question C7).
- Read-back: create returns only an Id (Guide: Responses & errors "Requests that create or update an entity return only its identifier"), so returning a Horus-generated number (AutoGenerateNumber, available only with Confirmed=true) costs one GET /book-entries.info call.

Connector-chosen safeguards, not reasons for the verdict: the closure-date check on fiscal-years.list before every create (Guide: Data model "Before pushing entries, check the relevant closure dates with fiscal-years.list"), the D12 duplicate pre-check on book-entries.list when operation_number is supplied (Horus documents no idempotency key) and the optional account and partner pre-validations. Reference data (daybooks, cost schemas and sections) is cached per folder.

Not a loss: line_number. Chift uses it only to order the lines ("This is used to order the lines in the operation"); the connector sends the lines in that order and echoes the values in the response. Whether Horus stores the array order as OrderNo is to confirm (A). partner_id on a general_account line is dropped, but it has no accounting meaning there (Guide: CompanyId "Not used" for Type 3).

horus_endpoints.role: Called before every create with Filter.Dates=[operation_date] and Filter.IncludeFuture=true, for two uses. (a) Closed-period pre-check, run before every create, as Horus recommends ('Before pushing entries, check the relevant closure dates with fiscal-years.list'): a fiscal year must contain operation_date, and the date must fall strictly after LastMiscOperationsClosureDate. Whether LastVatClosureDate also blocks miscellaneous operations is undocumented (open point). (b) When operation_number is supplied, the StartDate/EndDate of that fiscal year give the StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear period of the book-entries.list duplicate pre-check (D12). The comparison rule is a deduction (D), and the field is an untyped string|null, so it must be parsed defensively. The connector can then refuse or warn cleanly instead of relying on an undocumented Horus error. Closure dates are read fresh at each create, not from the reference cache, because the accountant can close a period at any time.

call_sequence: 0. [CHIFT_INTERNAL] Map consumer_id to the Horus licence connection: licence-specific api_url plus Bearer token, refreshed once on 401. Resolve FolderId with the shared folder rule (D7): use query folder_id when given (rejected with 400 'folder not selected for this connection' if it is not in the activation selection); if it is null and exactly one folder was selected at activation, use that folder; if no selection is stored, use the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0} (cached); otherwise return 400 'folder_id required'. Any Horus 403 is returned as Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details (D7).

1. [Connector validation, no Horus call] Reject the request before calling Horus when any of these holds: currency != 'EUR' and currency_exchange_rate is null, ≤ 0 or exactly 1 (422); lines is empty; a customer_account/supplier_account line has no partner_id; operation_number is present but not purely numeric, does not round-trip after conversion (leading zeros, more than 15 digits), or equals 0; after normalisation (conversion to EUR when currency != 'EUR', then rounding of each amount to 2 decimals) the lines do not balance (422; no automatic residue adjustment unless Chift defines a residue rule). Step 6 uses these same normalised amounts for Debit/Credit and CostLines.

2. [Journal] If journal_id is given: validate it against the cached daybooks.list, or GET /daybooks.info?Id=journal_id, and require Data.Folder.Id == FolderId (D13, otherwise 400) and Type == 600 (MiscOperation, D6). Daybooks of Type 610/690/700 are listed by Get journals as miscellaneous_operation with blocked=true (A), so they are rejected with 400 too. If journal_id is null: POST /daybooks.list {FolderId, Filter:{Types:[600]}}. Exactly one result → that is the DaybookId; otherwise return an error. Chift rule: 'automatically set if only one journal exists otherwise an error will be thrown'. This matches Get journals, where Type 600 is the only non-blocked miscellaneous_operation type (D6).

3. [Analytics, only if a line has analytic_account] GET /folders.info (cached) → WithAnalytics must be true. Resolve each analytic_account (a Horus cost-section GUID Id, D8) only from the per-folder analytics cache: POST /cost-schemas.list once per folder, plus POST /cost-sections.list per List-type (CostSectionType 100) schema with Filter.IncludeInactive=true. Make no per-call cost-sections.info / cost-schemas.info lookups (D8). An id that is not in the cache (unknown, a section of another folder, or anything outside a List-type schema) → 400; a section with Inactive=true → 422 (D8). Keep the section SearchKey (Value), the parent schema SearchKey (SchemaSearchKey) and the folder's Mandatory schemas.

4. [Fiscal year and pre-checks]
- Fiscal year: POST /fiscal-years.list {FolderId, Filter:{Dates:[operation_date as ISO 8601], IncludeFuture:true}}. Always called: it gives the closure dates for the pre-check (read fresh at each create, not from the reference cache) and, when operation_number is supplied, the period of the step-5 duplicate check (StartDate/EndDate → StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear) (D12). Refuse or warn only if no fiscal year comes back even with IncludeFuture=true; Horus's own behaviour in that case is undocumented ('?'). Require operation_date strictly after LastMiscOperationsClosureDate (D); that field is an untyped string|null, so parse it defensively. Whether LastVatClosureDate also blocks miscellaneous operations is undocumented: flag it, do not reject on it. GET /fiscal-years.info returns IsClosed (a year found closed can be cached).
- Accounts: POST /accounts.list {FolderId, Filter:{SearchKeys:[distinct account_numbers]}}. The filter is starts-with, so require an exact SearchKey match. Flag Inactive and IsSummary accounts; whether Horus refuses them is '?'. Flag general_account lines whose account is a customer or supplier concentration account (cached companies.list concentration accounts, or IntCategory 'COLLECCUS').
- Partners: for each distinct partner_id, POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{Id}} (folder-scoped by FolderId). If GET /companies.info is used instead, require Data.Folder.Id == FolderId, otherwise 400 (D13). Check that the company exists and is IsCustomer (Type 1) or IsSupplier (Type 2). Optionally compare account_number with the company's Customer/SupplierConcentrationAccount, resolved to a SearchKey ('?').

5. [Duplicate pre-check, D12: whenever operation_number is supplied, drafts included] POST /book-entries.list {FolderId, DaybookId, StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear = fiscal year from step 4, Filter:{DocumentNo: Number}}. Compare DocumentNo exactly on the client side. A match → reject with 400 (or 409, per C6) 'operation_number already exists in this journal and fiscal year' (with the existing book entry Id in the message) and do not create. Treating daybook + fiscal year as the uniqueness scope of Number is an assumption (A): Horus does not document Number uniqueness. The check is best effort: two identical calls in flight can both pass it; a connector-side lock per folder, daybook and number narrows that window (proposal).

6. [Build payload] Sort lines by line_number (stable sort). For each line:
- Type from type.
- Account = account_number.
- normalised amount (step 1) > 0 → Credit = amount, Debit = 0; < 0 → Debit = -amount, Credit = 0.
- Comment = description.
- CompanyId = partner_id, only for Type 1/2.
- If analytic_account: CostLines = [{Amount: |normalised amount|, Costs: [{SchemaSearchKey, Value: section SearchKey}]}], both keys from the D8 cache. A single cost line carries 100% of the line, so the D8 largest-remainder rounding rule is trivially exact.
Header: FolderId, DaybookId, Date = operation_date + 'T00:00:00+00:00'.
Status and number cases (D12):
- review mode (proposed default, D12), any status → Confirmed=false, Number = operation_number or 0; AutoGenerateNumber is not sent (it "Only works if "Confirmed" is set to *true*"); response status 'draft'.
- direct mode, draft → Confirmed=false, Number = operation_number or 0.
- direct mode, posted with a number → Confirmed=true, Number = operation_number.
- direct mode, posted without a number → Confirmed=true, AutoGenerateNumber=true, Number=0.
7. Record timestamp T0 just before the call, with a safety margin for clock skew. Then POST /book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new (Content-Type: application/json) → {Id}.

8. [Read-back, conditional: only when AutoGenerateNumber was used] GET /book-entries.info?Id=Id: one call, no FolderId, DaybookId or period. Check Data.Folder.Id == FolderId and Data.Daybook.Id == DaybookId (D13). A mismatch on an Id this call has just created is logged as an alert and the read-back data is not used; the request is not failed, because the operation exists. If the read-back times out or returns 404/500, never re-create and never return an error: build the response from the request (step 9), log the failure and retry the read-back later with backoff. Take DocumentNo, Confirmed, Date, Daybook.Id and the AccountHistories[] references.
Only if full line fidelity is wanted (book-entries.info returns line references only and is not a sideloading endpoint): POST /account-histories.list {FolderId, StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear = month of operation_date, Filter:{BookEntryId: Id, IncludeReport:false, IncludeCompanyDetail:true, IncludeCostDetail:true}} → OrderNo, AccountSearchKey, Debit, Credit, Comment, AccountType, CompanyDetail.Company.Id and CostDetail. Compare the returned Ids with the AccountHistories references (D; whether that array includes IsReport lines is '?').
If lines are missing: GET /account-histories.info?Id=<one reference> → AccountingMonth/AccountingYear, then repeat account-histories.list with that exact period, or resolve each missing reference with account-histories.info (1 call per line). account-histories.info has no Folder field: call it only on references from the verified book-entries.info and check Data.BookEntry.Id == Id (D13).

9. Build MiscellaneousOperationOut: id = Id; journal_id = the DaybookId used (equal to Daybook.Id when read back); status from the Confirmed value actually sent (so 'draft' in review mode, D12), or from book-entries.info when read back; operation_number = Number, or DocumentNo from book-entries.info, as a string (null if 0); operation_date = request date (or book-entries.info Date as YYYY-MM-DD); lines echoed from the request, or rebuilt from the line read-back; currency and currency_exchange_rate: when lines are echoed from the request, echo the request currency and rate with the request amounts; when lines are rebuilt from the read-back (EUR amounts), currency = 'EUR' and currency_exchange_rate = 1. EUR amounts are never paired with a foreign code (D4); final choice per Chift's answer on foreign-currency operations. When the read-back failed: id, journal_id, the status actually sent, operation_number = the supplied value or null (auto-generated, not yet read), lines echoed from the request.
Error mapping (map on Horus ErrorType, the machine-readable category, not on Message):
- 400 → Chift 400/422 with Horus Details; do not retry.
- 401 → refresh the token once and retry; if it fails again, ask the user to reconnect.
- 403 → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' (D7), with the Horus Details appended, because on this endpoint a 403 may also come from user rights (e.g. confirming entries). The Chift contract declares only 400/422/404. No retry.
- 404 → Chift 404.
- 500 or timeout → never blind-retry (D12; Horus has no idempotency key). First run a duplicate check (GET /book-entries.info cannot help, because the Id is lost with the response): book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo when the number is known; otherwise book-entries.list (DaybookId + period) or account-histories.list (DaybookIds) with Filter.ModifiedAfter=T0, comparing date, accounts and amounts. With a known number, retry with exponential backoff only if no match is found. If the check is inconclusive (no number and no unique match on date, accounts and amounts), return an outcome-unknown error instead of retrying.

limitations.impact: Line order is preserved through the order of the array (assumed to become OrderNo); the literal line_number values are not stored.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: The single Chift analytic_account ('no distribution possible') maps to one cost section in one List-type cost schema. Horus supports up to 8 schemas, distribution keys and Free (type 900) schemas; Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8).
limitations.impact: Folders with several Mandatory cost schemas, or with a Mandatory Free schema, cannot be fully served from the Chift input. Whether Horus rejects such lines is undocumented.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Partner information is meaningful only on Type 1/2 lines; CompanyId is 'Not used' for Type 3.
limitations.impact: A partner_id sent on a general_account line is dropped.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Only daybook Type 600 is documented as the target of this endpoint (D6).
limitations.impact: The connector auto-selects and accepts only Type 600 journals. Get journals lists 610 TemporaryMiscOperation, 690 SystemMiscOperation and 700 CostMiscOperation as miscellaneous_operation but with blocked=true (A), so a journal_id pointing to them is rejected with 400 until Horus confirms they can be posted to.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: No idempotency key in Horus write endpoints.
limitations.impact: A retry after a timeout can create a duplicate, so the connector never blind-retries (D12). Whenever operation_number is supplied, a book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo pre-check runs before the create (D12; the daybook + fiscal-year uniqueness scope is an assumption), and the same exact check runs after a timeout. With auto-numbering, detection after a timeout is only heuristic: query entries in the daybook/period with ModifiedAfter = pre-POST timestamp and compare date, accounts and amounts. Concurrent postings by other users can blur the result, so an inconclusive check returns an outcome-unknown error instead of a retry. The protection is best effort: two identical calls in flight can both pass the pre-check.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Status values 'matched' and 'cancelled' cannot result from this create call.
limitations.impact: The create response is always 'draft' or 'posted'.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: MiscOperation lines have no beneficiary line type (only 1 customer, 2 supplier, 3 general), although Horus beneficiaries (e.g. employees) are Companies and wages daybooks (IsWages) exist.
limitations.impact: Low impact for Chift, which has no employee line type either. Payroll ODs needing per-employee sub-ledger detail cannot be represented through this route. Whether a beneficiary Company may be referenced by CompanyId on a Type 1/2 line is undocumented.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Every create makes one live fiscal-years.list call for the closure check (closure dates are read fresh). A create that carries an operation_number makes one more before posting: the book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo duplicate pre-check (D12), over the fiscal year returned by the closure check.
limitations.impact: Slightly higher latency on every create, and more on numbered operations. Both pre-checks are safeguards chosen by the connector (Horus recommends the closure check; no idempotency key is documented), not Horus constraints, and are not reasons for the verdict. The duplicate pre-check assumes Number is unique per daybook and fiscal year, which Horus does not document.
limitations.label: D

edge_cases.case: Lines do not balance (sum of Chift amounts != 0), including floating-point drift
edge_cases.handling: Normalise each amount once (convert when needed, round to 2 decimals), check the balance on the normalised values, and send exactly those values. Reject with 422 if they do not balance: for example 33.333 + 33.333 − 66.666 balances as sent but not after rounding, and 10.004 − 10.001 balances after rounding but not as sent. Horus would return 400 (Guide: 'unbalanced entry'). No automatic residue adjustment unless Chift defines one.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: customer_account/supplier_account line without partner_id
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 422: Horus CompanyId is "Required if type = 1 or type = 2".
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: partner_id given on a general_account line
edge_cases.handling: Do not send CompanyId (guide: 'Not used'). Optionally warn that the partner link is lost.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: partner_id is a company that is not flagged IsCustomer (Type 1) or IsSupplier (Type 2)
edge_cases.handling: Pre-validate with companies.list and reject or warn. Horus behaviour is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: customer_account/supplier_account line whose account_number differs from the partner's CustomerConcentrationAccount/SupplierConcentrationAccount (or is a P&L/general account)
edge_cases.handling: Optionally pre-validate: companies.list → concentration account Id → SearchKey via cached accounts.list (or GET /accounts.info, accepted only if Data.Folder.Id = FolderId, D13); then warn or reject. Ask Horus whether it refuses, accepts or overrides the account.

edge_cases.case: general_account line whose account_number is a customer or supplier concentration account (a CustomerConcentrationAccount/SupplierConcentrationAccount in the cached companies.list, or IntCategory 'COLLECCUS')
edge_cases.handling: Warn or reject according to Chift policy. The line would be stored as a general line (Type 3 → AccountType 300, D) without a company, so the collective balance moves without a third party and company-level open items cannot explain it. Whether Horus accepts it is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: status=posted and operation_number null, direct mode
edge_cases.handling: Confirmed=true, AutoGenerateNumber=true, Number=0. Read DocumentNo back via GET /book-entries.info?Id=<returned Id>, used only if Data.Folder.Id = FolderId (D13). If that read-back fails or shows another folder, return operation_number null and retry later (see the read-back edge case).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: status=draft and operation_number null
edge_cases.handling: Confirmed=false, Number=0. Response operation_number=null. No business key until the accountant confirms it: an edit before confirmation gives a new id that the consumer cannot reconcile (C7) (D).
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: operation_number is non-numeric (e.g. 'OD-2024-001')
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 422 (Number is a number type; proposal, C7). Do not silently fall back to auto-numbering; the alternative in C7 (Horus numbers confirmed operations and the client value is kept in the line comment) needs a Chift decision.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: operation_number with leading zeros ('000123') or a very long digit string
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 422: numeric conversion drops leading zeros ('000123' → 123) and more than 15 digits risks precision loss in JSON numbers (proposal; C7).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: operation_number = '0'
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 422: Number 0 means 'no number' in Horus ('can be 0 if not confirmed'), and the D12 pre-check would match every unnumbered entry.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: journal_id null and several Type 600 daybooks (e.g. a general OD daybook plus a wages daybook, IsWages=true)
edge_cases.handling: Return an error as the Chift contract requires. Only Type 600 daybooks are counted (D6), so blocked 610/690/700 journals never make auto-selection fail. Optionally offer a connector setting for a default daybook.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: journal_id points to a non-600 daybook (sales, bank, or a 610/690/700 misc daybook)
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400 after daybooks.info/daybooks.list validation. This includes 610/690/700 daybooks, which Get journals shows as miscellaneous_operation with blocked=true (D6; A until Horus confirms whether they accept this endpoint).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: currency ≠ EUR
edge_cases.handling: Convert at currency_exchange_rate (Chift core or connector, per Chift's answer). A missing rate, a rate ≤ 0 or exactly 1 → 422. A rounding residue that unbalances the entry → 422 unless Chift defines a residue rule. The response never pairs EUR amounts with a foreign code (D4).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: operation_date in a closed period (on or before LastMiscOperationsClosureDate, or fiscal year IsClosed)
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check with fiscal-years.list/info before every create, closure dates read fresh, and reject. 'Strictly after the closure date' is a deduction (the closure date is taken as the last closed day). LastMiscOperationsClosureDate is an untyped string|null, so parse it defensively. Horus's own error in this case is undocumented. Whether a VAT closure (LastVatClosureDate) also blocks operations is undocumented; flag it, do not reject on it, until Horus answers.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: operation_date in a fiscal year that fiscal-years.list hides by default (a 'future' year, e.g. early postings into next year's exercise)
edge_cases.handling: Always send Filter.IncludeFuture=true in the pre-check. Do not reject just because the default list is empty.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: No fiscal year contains operation_date even with IncludeFuture=true
edge_cases.handling: Reject or warn, according to Chift policy. Horus's own behaviour and error are undocumented. If the operation is not rejected and operation_number is supplied, the D12 pre-check has no fiscal-year period: use the calendar year of operation_date (A).

edge_cases.case: analytic_account given but folder WithAnalytics=false, or the id is not in the folder's analytics cache (unknown, a section of another folder, or not a List-type section)
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400. Ids are resolved only from the folder-scoped cache (D8), so a section of another folder is 'not found' (D13). For WithAnalytics=false, dropping the analytic link with a warning remains an option if Chift prefers leniency.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: analytic_account resolves to an Inactive cost section
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 422 (D8). Inactive is read from the cache built with cost-sections.list IncludeInactive=true (the default FALSE would make it look 'unknown'). Whether Horus itself would accept the section is undocumented, but the connector rejects first.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Folder has additional Mandatory cost schemas beyond the one implied by analytic_account
edge_cases.handling: Unknown whether Horus rejects the line. Pre-detect via the cached cost-schemas.list (Mandatory, D8), warn, and flag it to Horus.

edge_cases.case: Line with amount = 0
edge_cases.handling: Send Debit=0, Credit=0 (acceptance undocumented), or drop the line after agreement with Chift.

edge_cases.case: Account requires a vehicle (car expenses) but Chift provides none
edge_cases.handling: Send without VehicleId. Whether Horus refuses is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: Unknown account_number
edge_cases.handling: Pre-validate with accounts.list, using an exact SearchKey match because the filter is starts-with. Otherwise Horus returns 400 (Guide: Responses & errors 'unknown account').
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: account_number resolves to an account with Inactive=true or IsSummary=true
edge_cases.handling: Pre-validate with the cached accounts.list and reject or warn. Confirm the posting rule with Horus.

edge_cases.case: Horus returns 403 (user/integrator not allowed, e.g. no access to the folder, or an entrepreneur connection trying to post or confirm)
edge_cases.handling: Do not retry. Return Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' (D7; the Chift contract declares no 403), appending the Horus Details because a 403 here may also come from user rights. Use ErrorType for classification. The exact causes of a 403 on this endpoint are undocumented.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Timeout or 500 after POST (the entry may have been created)
edge_cases.handling: Never blind-retry (D12). Before retrying: with a known number, search book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo. With auto-numbering, query book-entries.list (DaybookId + period) or account-histories.list (DaybookIds) with Filter.ModifiedAfter = timestamp recorded just before the POST, and compare date, accounts and amounts. This is a heuristic, because concurrent postings by others are possible. GET /book-entries.info cannot help here, because the Id is lost with the response. If the check is inconclusive (no number and no unique match on date, accounts and amounts), return an outcome-unknown error instead of retrying.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line read-back period: account-histories.list filters by month/year, and the accounting month may differ from the calendar month of Date
edge_cases.handling: The header read-back (GET /book-entries.info) needs no period. For lines, use the month of operation_date. If the Id is not found or references are missing, read AccountingMonth/AccountingYear from GET /account-histories.info on one AccountHistories reference and repeat with that exact period, or resolve each reference with account-histories.info.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Duplicate or missing line_number values (default 1 on every line)
edge_cases.handling: A stable sort keeps input order.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: operation_number already exists in the target daybook within the fiscal year (D12 pre-check match)
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400 (or 409, per C6) 'operation_number already exists in this journal and fiscal year' before creating, with the existing book entry Id in the message. Treating daybook + fiscal year as the uniqueness scope is an assumption; Horus does not document Number uniqueness.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: status=posted in review mode (proposed default, D12)
edge_cases.handling: Send Confirmed=false. AutoGenerateNumber cannot be used ("Only works if "Confirmed" is set to *true*"), so without operation_number Number=0 and operation_number is returned null. Return status 'draft' so the response reflects what Horus stored.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: journal_id or partner_id that belongs to another folder of the same licence
edge_cases.handling: journal_id: daybooks.info Data.Folder.Id ≠ FolderId → 400 (D13). partner_id: companies.list is folder-scoped by FolderId; if companies.info is used, Data.Folder.Id ≠ FolderId → 400 (D13). Without pre-validation, Horus's behaviour for a CompanyId of another folder is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Folder has a Mandatory Free schema (CostSectionType 900)
edge_cases.handling: Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8), so no value can be sent for them. Warn. Whether Horus rejects the line is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: Read-back fails after a successful create (GET /book-entries.info times out, returns 404 or 500, or shows another folder)
edge_cases.handling: Never re-create and never return an error: the operation exists, and a confirmed one cannot be deleted through the API. Return the Id with the status sent, operation_number = the supplied value (null if Horus generated it) and the echoed lines; log the failure and retry the read-back later with backoff. A folder mismatch on a just-created Id is an alert, not a Chift 400.
edge_cases.label: D

open_questions.question: Is the folder base currency always EUR (BE/LU legislations)? Is a currency field for miscellaneous operations planned? How many decimals do Debit and Credit accept, and is the balance checked on the exact values sent?
open_questions.why: The misc-op schema has no CurrencyCode/CurrencyRate, so foreign-currency operations are converted to the folder currency at the supplied rate; this assumes the folder currency is EUR. The connector rounds to 2 decimals before the balance check.

open_questions.question: Is Number unique per daybook or fiscal year? Is a format enforced (the documented examples differ: 201909001, 1904001, 2301016)? What happens on a duplicate? How does AutoGenerateNumber choose the next number when manually numbered entries exist, and must a manually supplied Number on a confirmed entry follow the daybook's sequence or format?
open_questions.why: Needed to map Chift operation_number safely and to scope the D12 duplicate pre-check (book-entries.list Filter.DocumentNo over the daybook and fiscal year), which currently assumes daybook + fiscal-year uniqueness.

open_questions.question: Can every integration or licence set Confirmed=true, or can the fiduciary restrict this? Can a connection authorised by an entrepreneur (IsAccountant=false) post and confirm miscellaneous operations, or will Horus return 403? Does confirmation also lock edits through .update and .lines.update? Is Confirmed the accountant's final validation, or does Verified follow it where an extra verification step is configured?
open_questions.why: Chift's default status is 'posted', and confirmed entries cannot be deleted through the API. This determines whether direct posting mode (D12) is available for SMB-licence connections and how to map a 403. (Consolidated in section 9 as the Horus question on confirmation rights.)

open_questions.question: Which daybook types does book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new accept: only 600, or also 610 TemporaryMiscOperation and wages daybooks (IsWages)?
open_questions.why: Determines which journals the connector exposes as valid targets and how journal auto-selection behaves. Until answered, D6 accepts only 600 and marks 610/690/700 as blocked (A).

open_questions.question: Are CostLines accepted on Type 1/2 lines and on balance-sheet accounts? What happens if the folder has several Mandatory cost schemas and only one is provided, or if a Mandatory schema is Free (CostSectionType 900)? What value format do Free schemas take in CostLines?
open_questions.why: Chift sends one analytic_account per line; we need to know when Horus will reject. Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8) until this is answered.

open_questions.question: Does Horus enforce that a Type 1/2 line uses the company's customer/supplier concentration account? Can posting target Inactive or summary (IsSummary) accounts?
open_questions.why: Chift sends account_number freely; these rules drive pre-validation and error mapping.

open_questions.question: What is the error (ErrorType) when posting into a closed period or outside any fiscal year, on an account requiring a vehicle without VehicleId, or with a zero-amount line? Is there a list of ErrorType values?
open_questions.why: Needed for pre-validation and for mapping errors to Chift 400/422.

open_questions.question: What is the format of LastMiscOperationsClosureDate, and is posting on that exact date allowed? Which fiscal years count as 'future' for IncludeFuture? Does a VAT closure (LastVatClosureDate) block miscellaneous operations dated on or before it?
open_questions.why: Needed for an exact closed-period and fiscal-year pre-check.

open_questions.question: Is the order of the Lines array persisted as OrderNo? Is the AccountHistories array of GET /book-entries.info ordered by OrderNo, and does it include IsReport lines? Could sideloading of AccountHistories be enabled on book-entries.info?
open_questions.why: Line order must be preserved for Chift line_number. The reference list is used to check that a line read-back is complete, and sideloading would return the entry and its lines in one call without a period (Guide: Sideloading "If you need it on another endpoint, contact us").

open_questions.question: Does the book entry Id also change when the accountant edits an entry in Horus Office (not only through API updates)? Does confirming an entry keep its Id and Number, and does an edited entry keep its DocumentNo?
open_questions.why: Affects the stability of the id returned to Chift and of GET-by-id routes.

open_questions.question: D12 proposes a posting mode chosen per connection at activation: review (every operation pushed unconfirmed; proposed default) or direct (Confirmed=true for 'posted'). Is that acceptable, and should the mode be settable per folder?
open_questions.why: Product decision (D12): Horus pushes API entries unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, while Chift defaults to 'posted', and confirmed entries cannot be deleted through the API. (Consolidated as C1.)

open_questions.question: Is operation_number meant to be the accounting entry number or the client's own reference? Should non-numeric values be rejected, or should confirmed operations be numbered by Horus (AutoGenerateNumber) with the client value kept in the line comment? Is rejecting values with leading zeros acceptable?
open_questions.why: The Chift field has no description; Horus numbers are numeric, and Horus can number confirmed operations itself. (Consolidated as C7; foreign-currency operations: see the Chift question on foreign-currency operations in section 9.)

open_questions.question: Please confirm the D8 convention for this route: analytic_account is the Horus cost-section GUID Id exposed by Get analytic accounts, and Free (900) schemas are neither exposed nor accepted in v1. Is a 400 on an unknown id (and a 422 on an inactive section) acceptable, or should the connector drop the analytic link with a warning?
open_questions.why: D8 fixes the id convention across routes; the remaining choice is the error policy for analytic ids that cannot be resolved.

open_questions.question: D6 maps 600/610/690/700 to miscellaneous_operation, with 610/690/700 blocked=true, and this route auto-selects only Type 600. Should IsWages (Type 600) daybooks be excluded from auto-selection, given that a wages daybook next to a general OD daybook makes auto-selection fail?
open_questions.why: The 'only one journal' rule must match what Get journals exposes as non-blocked. Wages daybooks are Type 600 and therefore not blocked.

open_questions.question: Does Chift core already validate line balance and partner_id presence, or must the connector do it? Is the D7 mapping of every Horus 403 to 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)', with the Horus Details, acceptable, given that the Chift contract declares no 403? Should a general line on a customer or supplier concentration account be rejected or accepted with a warning?
open_questions.why: Avoids duplicated or missing validation and fixes the error codes.

open_questions.question: When an operation arrives in a currency other than EUR with currency_exchange_rate, does Chift core convert the amounts before calling the connector (as other_currencies_allowed = false suggests: 'for Chift to convert the amounts'), or must the connector convert? In which direction is the rate expressed? How should a rounding residue on a balanced operation be absorbed? Should the response echo the original currency and rate, or EUR with rate 1?
open_questions.why: Horus stores operations in EUR only; the Chift contract requires the rate for operations in another currency and describes conversion for journals that do not allow other currencies.

open_questions.question: Do clients expect the literal line_number values (for example 10/20/30) to come back on later reads, or only the line order?
open_questions.why: Horus has no writable line number; only the order of the lines is expected to be kept (OrderNo, to confirm with Horus).

open_questions.question: Does Chift core retry create calls automatically after a 5xx or timeout? Is a 200 with operation_number null acceptable when Horus generated the number but the read-back failed?
open_questions.why: After a successful create the connector returns the operation rather than an error, so that no retry books it twice.

open_questions.question: Is GET /book-entries.info immediately consistent after book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.new returns its Id?
open_questions.why: The read-back runs immediately after the create.

evidence_gaps: GET /book-entries.info is documented (query Id only; returns DocumentNo, Confirmed, Date, Daybook.Id and AccountHistories Type/Id references) but carries no line content, and it is not in the guide's list of sideloading endpoints. The order of its AccountHistories array, and whether that array includes IsReport lines, are not documented.
No documentation of Number uniqueness, format or sequencing rules per daybook.
No documentation of the folder base currency, or of whether misc operations can carry a foreign currency (only invoices have CurrencyCode).

No documented Horus error for posting into closed periods or outside any fiscal year; the guide only advises checking closure dates. Whether LastVatClosureDate also blocks miscellaneous operations is not stated. The format of LastMiscOperationsClosureDate (string|null, no example) and the meaning of 'future' in fiscal-years.list IncludeFuture are not documented.

No documentation of mandatory cost-schema enforcement, of CostLines on customer/supplier lines, of free (type 900) schemas in CostLines, or of posting on Inactive cost sections. Free schemas are therefore excluded in v1 (D8).
No documentation of whether Type 1/2 lines must use the company's concentration account, or whether Inactive/IsSummary accounts can be posted to.
No documentation of the 'account requires a vehicle' rule or its error.
No confirmation that the order of the Lines array is persisted as OrderNo.
No list of ErrorType values; only the format {ErrorType, Details, Message} is documented. The specific causes of 403 on this endpoint are not described.
Sideloading the AccountHistories array on book-entries.list is not documented (only the Include mechanism and the supported endpoints are).
Quickstart, Register your integration, Support & FAQ, Changelog, Postman collection and webhook docs were not provided. Rate limits and idempotency guidance, if any, are unknown.
Whether Confirmed=true can be restricted per licence or user type (accountant vs entrepreneur) is not documented.
Whether .update / .lines.update work on confirmed entries is not stated (only delete is explicitly limited to non-confirmed).

book-entries.list states that "All filters on *strings* are performed using the *contains* clause" but does not say how the numeric Filter.DocumentNo matches, so the D12 pre-check compares DocumentNo exactly on the client side.

POST /cost-sections.info takes only an Id and returns no Folder field, and GET /account-histories.info returns no Folder field either. Cross-folder checks (D13) for these objects therefore rely on the folder-scoped cache (D8) and on verified parent references.

No documentation of whether a create that timed out on the client side can still be committed afterwards, or of whether book-entries.list and book-entries.info show a new entry as soon as the create call has returned. The duplicate check after a timeout is therefore best effort.
ba_insights:
Terminology map (each meaning taken from the Horus docs):
- Horus Folder = Chift folder: the legal entity whose books are kept.
- Horus Company = a third-party legal entity the folder deals with (customer, supplier or beneficiary) = Chift partner. The folder's own entity is the Folder.
- Daybook = Chift journal: the posting target, chosen by Type; 600 = MiscOperation.
- Account = ledger account, referenced by its search key.
- Book entry = the operation header (Chift id).
- Account history = one entry line.
- Cost schema = analytic plan; cost section = analytic account.
- MatchNo = matching (lettering) number.

Why more than one call: Horus create endpoints return only an Id (Guide: Responses & errors "Requests that create or update an entity return only its identifier"), while Chift expects the full object back. Horus also references accounts and analytics by search key (Guide: Data model "Accounts and cost schemas/sections are referenced by search key in posting endpoints"), while Chift sends an analytic account id. Hence lookup → create → (conditional) read-back. Reference lookups should be cached per folder (Guide: Reading accounting data "Load it once and cache it per folder").

Read-back by Id: GET /book-entries.info?Id= needs only the Id that create returns (no FolderId, DaybookId or period) and gives DocumentNo, Confirmed, Date, Daybook.Id and the line references. That is the cheapest way to return operation_number after auto-numbering. Lines come back only as references, so full line fidelity needs one account-histories.list call (Filter.BookEntryId) or one account-histories.info per line. book-entries.list is kept for duplicate checks, where the Id is unknown. Use the read-back only if its Folder.Id matches the request folder (D13). A mismatch or a failed read-back is logged and never fails the request, because the operation exists.

Sign trap: Chift uses one signed amount (positive = Credit, negative = Debit). Horus uses two non-negative columns, Debit and Credit, which are both mandatory. Horus validates balance ('must be balanced') and, unlike invoices, has no AllowUnbalanced escape hatch on ODs. Validate in the connector to return a clean 422 instead of a Horus 400. Normalise amounts once (conversion when needed, 2-decimal rounding) and check the balance on exactly the values sent.

Line-type trap: Horus Type 1/2 lines identify the sub-ledger through CompanyId and, in the guide's example, post on the collective account (400000). Type 3 ignores CompanyId. So Chift 'type' plus 'partner_id' drive two Horus fields, and a partner on a general line is lost. Whether Horus enforces the company's concentration account is undocumented.

Status trap: Chift defaults to 'posted' ('finalized'); Horus pushes API entries unconfirmed so the accountant can review them, and Confirmed means validated by the accountant. The sources do not equate the two. D12 proposes a per-connection posting mode: review (push unconfirmed, proposed default) or direct (Confirmed=true for 'posted'). Confirmed=true removes the API delete option (delete only for "non-confirmed, and have been injected through the API"). In review mode AutoGenerateNumber is unavailable, so an unnumbered operation comes back without a number. Decision owner: Chift (C1).

Numbering: Number is numeric and can be 0 while unconfirmed. AutoGenerateNumber works only with Confirmed=true (Number left at 0). A posted operation without a Chift number in direct mode therefore needs a read-back to return operation_number. An unconfirmed operation (draft, or review mode) without a number has none to return. operation_number is assumed to be the entry number; values with leading zeros, and the value 0, are rejected (proposal, C7).

Id stability: every book-entries.*.update returns a new book entry Id and deletes the attachment. Chift-side storage and GET-by-id routes should also reconcile on daybook + DocumentNo (Guide: Reading accounting data).

Currency: the Chift contract makes 'currency' required, but Horus ODs have no currency field (unlike invoices), so amounts are stored in EUR. Chift's own contract describes conversion for journals that do not allow other currencies ('an exchange rate must be provided for Chift to convert the amounts to the journal currency'), and Get journals returns other_currencies_allowed = false for Type 600 daybooks. Foreign-currency ODs are therefore converted at the supplied rate, not rejected; whether Chift core or the connector converts is a question for Chift. The original currency is not kept in Horus. State this plainly to clients.

Analytics (D8): Chift analytic_account (a cost-section GUID, 'no distribution possible') becomes one CostLine whose Amount equals the line's debit/credit amount, with Costs = [{SchemaSearchKey, Value}]. Both search keys come from one per-folder cache (cost-schemas.list + cost-sections.list per List-type schema with IncludeInactive=true), never from per-call .info lookups. An inactive section is rejected with 422 and an unknown one with 400. Free (900) schemas are excluded in v1. Multi-dimension or mandatory-schema folders are a known risk to confirm with Horus.

Fiscal-year pre-check: fiscal-years.list hides future fiscal years by default (IncludeFuture FALSE). Always send IncludeFuture=true, or valid postings into next year's exercise will be wrongly rejected. Read the closure dates fresh at each create (one small call), because the accountant can close a period at any time.

Error handling (per Guide: Responses & errors), branching on ErrorType ("Use it in your code"):
- 400 → do not retry; surface Details (unknown account, unbalanced entry).
- 401 → refresh the token once.
